content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"Several conclusions can be traced to testimony, such as S1A's account of the telework hardship and the leave restriction rationale, but the ROI omits the DRAD file, medical records, leave records and FMLA file, so the path from evidence to conclusion is broken at key points."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Most characterizations are attributed to named sources (Complainant, S1A, S1B, EOD, DRAD1), but attendance and absenteeism claims, the PIP, and the HR recorded-voicemail allegation are not tied to any documents, and S1B's account of HR making the leave-restriction decision rests on recollection."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Many events are dated (Dec 21, 2017 request; Feb 9, 21 and Jun 4, 14, 2018 DRAD steps; Jun 7, 2018 leave restriction), but the sequence is muddled by conflicts over whether the PIP was imposed Sept 2017, when S1B became supervisor (April 2018 vs. other references), and whether the FMLA request was June or August 2018."},"rc4":{"status":"review","note":"The leave restriction names consultation with EOD and S1B and cites excessive absence as the rationale, but S1B attributes the decision to HR, the threshold applied is not documented, and there is no record that Complainant's responses were considered before finalization."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"Missing DRAD, FMLA and leave records, contradictory accounts of who decided the leave restriction and when the FMLA request arrived, and undocumented criteria mean an independent reviewer could not assess support for the conclusion without outside context."}}}
